responsibility:
`rustc_hir_analysis` performs semantic analysis on HIR after lowering, turning item declarations and type syntax into the compiler’s internal type information, checking that those definitions and uses are valid, and publishing the query results and diagnostics that later compiler phases rely on. The crate root `lib.rs` wires together the overall HIR-analysis pipeline and its queries for collection, coherence, body checking, variance, outlives, well-formedness, and delegation. Type and predicate metadata are established by the `collect` module and the root `collect.rs`, which drive item collection, lower signatures, generics, bounds, opaques, coroutine/delegation metadata, and related item-level type information into `rustc_middle::ty`. The `astconv` module performs the actual conversion from HIR/AST type syntax into internal `ty` representations, validating generic arguments, late-bound regions, type paths, bounds, `Fn`-trait syntax, associated items, and type bindings during lowering, while the root `bounds.rs` supplies the shared `Bounds` accumulator that stores the lowered predicates with ordering and span information.

Once items are collected, the `check` module coordinates the main semantic checking phase: item-level validation, trait/impl compatibility checks, drop-soundness rules, intrinsic and inline-assembly verification, region scope-tree construction, and whole-item well-formedness obligation solving. Supporting this, `hir_wf_check.rs` provides HIR-based fallback logic for finding the most precise source span when well-formedness predicate failures occur. Coherence for impls is handled by the `coherence` module, which enforces crate-wide rules for well-formed, non-conflicting trait and inherent impls, including orphan rules, unsafe impl requirements, built-in/lang-item trait contracts, inherent-impl collection, and inherent-item overlap detection. Impl-specific well-formedness is further enforced by both the root `impl_wf_check.rs` and the `impl_wf_check` module, which reject unconstrained impl parameters and validate specialization, especially `min_specialization`, by checking that specializing impls remain sound and compatible with their parents; `constrained_generic_params.rs` supports these checks by computing which generic parameters are actually determined by an impl header or predicate set.

The crate also computes global type-system properties needed by later analyses. The `outlives` module extracts explicit and infers implicit outlives requirements for type definitions, publishing item- and crate-level inferred outlives data through queries. The `variance` module infers generic-parameter variance by collecting parameter uses, generating and solving variance constraints, and exposing the results through queries and test hooks. User-facing error reporting is centralized by `errors.rs`, which declares the crate’s broad catalog of diagnostics, lints, and subdiagnostics for semantic analysis failures, while the `structured_errors` module together with the root `structured_errors.rs` provides reusable structured-diagnostic builders and interfaces for specific context-sensitive errors such as variadic cast problems, thin-to-fat pointer cast failures, and wrong generic-argument counts. Finally, `check_unused.rs` contributes the query-backed pass that detects trait imports that were never used during type checking and emits the corresponding `unused_imports` lint. Together, these modules make `rustc_hir_analysis` the compiler component that converts HIR into checked type-system facts, enforces semantic and coherence rules on items and impls, infers key generic properties, and produces the diagnostics and lints associated with this stage.
